media.title: Tiger: Spy in the Jungle
media.plot: Hidden cameras follow four tiger cubs from birth through their first two years in Pench National Park, India.

media.title: Life of Pi
media.plot: A young man survives a disaster at sea and shares a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger named Richard Parker.

media.title: Tigers: Tracking a Legend
media.plot: Following conservationists working to protect the last wild tigers across fragmented habitats in Southeast Asia.

media.title: The Jungle Book
media.plot: Mowgli navigates the jungle with the menacing Bengal tiger Shere Khan as his primary adversary.

media.title: David Attenborough's Tiger
media.plot: Sir David Attenborough explores the remarkable adaptations and precarious future of wild tigers.

habitat.description: Tigers inhabit a remarkable diversity of environments, from the tropical rainforests of Sumatra to the snowy taiga of the Russian Far East. They require large territories with dense cover, access to water, and abundant prey. A single male tiger may patrol a territory exceeding 100 square kilometers.

threats.name: Habitat Loss
threats.description: Deforestation for palm oil, agriculture, and infrastructure has reduced tiger habitat by 95% over the last century.

threats.name: Poaching
threats.description: Illegal trade in tiger parts for traditional medicine and luxury goods drives systematic hunting despite international bans.

threats.name: Human-Wildlife Conflict
threats.description: As habitats shrink, tigers increasingly encounter human settlements, leading to retaliatory killings.

threats.name: Prey Depletion
threats.description: Overhunting of deer and wild boar by local communities reduces the prey base tigers depend upon.

conservationStatus.population: Approximately 4,500 individuals in the wild (2023 estimate)

culturalSignificance.overview: The tiger occupies an unparalleled place in human culture, serving as a symbol of power, beauty, and wildness across civilizations. From William Blake's 'Tyger Tyger, burning bright' to the national emblem of India and Bangladesh, the tiger represents nature's raw magnificence.
literature: The Jungle Book by Rudyard Kipling
Life of Pi by Yann Martel
culturalSignificance.symbolism: Emblem of courage, strength, and sovereignty. The tiger represents the untamed wilderness and humanity's complex relationship with apex predators.
